info.name: FoC Supplier Service (D2)
info.description: The Supplier Service D2 demo: query patterns, denied requests, and CRUD through the API alone. Import together with local.postman_environment.json; see api/README.md.

item.name: 0 Setup (log in)
item.description: Log in once as each demo user. Their tokens are stored in the environment (basicToken, adminToken) and sent as Authorization: Bearer by every Supplier Service request, so both users can be used side by side. Alternatively, paste tokens into the environment by hand.

request.description: Logs in at user-service and saves the access token as {{basicToken}}. The token arrives only as the httpOnly access_token cookie.
Logs in at user-service and saves the access token as {{adminToken}}. The token arrives only as the httpOnly access_token cookie.

item.name: 1 Query patterns (D2 point 2)
item.description: Any logged-in user may read (F13.3). Run as the basic user.

request.description: In-use buildings with names and coordinates (F4.4). Saves PGP and COM3 ids for later requests.
In-use categories (F11.4). Saves the Food and Coffee ids.
Paginated listing, sorted by display name then id (F5.1-F5.3, N3.1). Saves the first supplier's id.
Case-insensitive partial name match (F5.4.1).
Suppliers in a building: 'finding suppliers by location' (F5.4.3).
Suppliers with any of the given categories (F5.4.2).

exec: pm.test('all have Coffee', () => pm.response.json().items.forEach((s) => pm.expect(s.categories.map((c) => c.name)).to.include('Coffee')));

request.description: Filters combine with AND (F5.5); caller-chosen sort, id as final tie-breaker (F5.3.1).
Offset/limit paging (F5.2, N3.1).
All fields including version; the version is also the ETag (F5.9, F15.1).
A distinct not-found response (F5.9.1).
Unknown and malformed parameters are rejected, all listed at once (F5.8, N8.4.1).

item.name: 2 Denied requests (D2 points 2 and 4)
item.description: How denied requests are answered: no token → 401 (F13.2); a basic user on an admin action → 403, and nothing is changed (F13.5).

item.name: 3 CRUD as admin (D2 point 3)
item.description: Create, read, update and 'delete' (= set Inactive) through the API alone. Each run uses a fresh supplier name, so the folder can be re-run.

request.description: Admin-only direct create (F7.5): Active, version 1, with Location and ETag headers.
Same name, building and floor: rejected by the database's unique constraint (F1.5, F1.5.2).

item.name: Create with several problems (400, all listed)

request.description: Field rules, unknown references and system-managed fields are all reported in one response (F1.6.1, F1.3.2).
Any logged-in user can read it (F13.3).
An edit must state the version it is based on (F14.3).
Direct admin update of some fields (F8.6); the version goes up by 1 (F1.3.1).

exec: pm.test('fields changed', () => { pm.expect(s.locationDescription).to.eql('Opposite the lift'); pm.expect(s.categories.map((c) => c.name)).to.have.members(['Coffee', 'Food']); });

request.description: Someone else's change is not silently overwritten: conflict with the current version (F14.3.1).
Admin-only status change (F9.5). The supplier stays in the database, tagged Inactive; errands already created are unaffected (F9.6).

exec: pm.test('Inactive at version 3', () => { const s = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(s.status).to.eql('Inactive'); pm.expect(s.version).to.eql(3); });

request.description: Only Active <-> Inactive is allowed (F9.2).

item.name: Active list no longer shows it

request.description: Filtered by status Active (F5.4.5).
Inactive suppliers remain available in lookups (F5.7).

item.name: 4 Supplier requests (D2 points 3 and 4)
item.description: Moderated changes (F6, F7, F8): a basic user asks for a new supplier or an edit; an admin reviews, approves or denies; the user follows their own requests and may withdraw a pending one. Nothing changes until an admin approves.

item.name: Basic user asks to add a supplier (201, Pending)

request.description: Any logged-in user may file a request (F7.1, F13.3). It is validated exactly like an admin's create; the supplier does not exist yet.
An identical request is already Pending (F7.2), enforced by a partial unique index in the database.
Reviewing requests is admin-only (F13.4).
Pending requests, oldest first (F6.7).
Creates the supplier and records the approval in one transaction (F6.8). Duplicates are checked again at this moment (F7.3.1).

exec: pm.test('Approved, with who and when', () => { pm.expect(r.state).to.eql('Approved'); pm.expect(r.resolvedBy).to.be.ok; pm.expect(r.resolvedAt).to.be.ok; });

request.description: A request is resolved exactly once (F6.3).

item.name: Basic user asks to edit it (201, Pending)

request.description: Any logged-in user may propose an edit (F8.1), based on the version they saw (If-Match, as for an admin edit). Validated exactly like an admin PATCH.

exec: pm.test('Pending Update request on version 1', () => { pm.expect(r.type).to.eql('Update'); pm.expect(r.state).to.eql('Pending'); pm.expect(r.supplierVersion).to.eql(1); });
pm.test('only the changed field is recorded', () => pm.expect(r.values).to.eql({ locationDescription: 'Beside the vending machines, level 3 lobby' }));

item.name: Second edit for the same supplier (409)

request.description: A supplier has at most one pending edit (F8.3), enforced by a partial unique index.
F8.2: the listing keeps returning the live record until an admin approves.

exec: pm.test('still version 1, old description', () => { pm.expect(s.version).to.eql(1); pm.expect(s.locationDescription).to.eql('Beside the vending machines'); });

request.description: Applies the changes through the same code as an admin PATCH (F8.4). Refused with 409 VERSION_CONFLICT if the supplier changed since the request was filed (F8.4.1).

exec: pm.test('new description at version 2', () => { pm.expect(s.version).to.eql(2); pm.expect(s.locationDescription).to.eql('Beside the vending machines, level 3 lobby'); });

item.name: Basic user asks for another supplier

request.description: A denial needs a reason of 1-500 characters (F6.4).

exec: pm.test('Denied, with the reason', () => { pm.expect(r.state).to.eql('Denied'); pm.expect(r.denialReason).to.eql('Could not find it at COM3 level 4'); pm.expect(r.createdSupplierId).to.eql(null); });

request.description: The caller's own requests of every type and state, newest first, paged (F6.5). Filter with ?state= and ?type=.

exec: pm.test('newest first', () => { const t = page.items.map((r) => r.submittedAt); pm.expect(t).to.eql([...t].sort().reverse()); });
pm.test('includes the denial reason', () => pm.expect(byId[pm.environment.get('deniedRequestId')].denialReason).to.eql('Could not find it at COM3 level 4'));

item.name: Basic user views the denied request

request.description: One request, for its submitter or an admin. Anyone else gets 404, exactly as for an unknown id (F13.6).

exec: pm.test('Denied, with the reason', () => { const r = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(r.state).to.eql('Denied'); pm.expect(r.denialReason).to.be.a('string'); });

item.name: Basic user asks for a third supplier

request.description: Only the submitter may withdraw. To anyone else the request does not exist (F13.6); an admin rejects a request by denying it.
Withdraws the caller's own Pending request (F6.6). It leaves the admin queue, and the same request may be filed again.

item.name: Tidy up: read the approved supplier

request.description: The last two requests deactivate the demo supplier, so re-runs don't fill the Active list.
